facility_roles.note: Host selection announced 12 August 2024; the Steering Committee chose on 31 July 2024 to start detailed negotiations with Chile.
facility_roles.quote: announced that the Atacama Astronomical Park in Chile was selected as the site of the observatory.

intervals.label: R&D collaboration; observatory proposed
intervals.note: The status is proposed: the 2025 science paper says planning for construction in Chile "has begun" and no source consulted reports construction started. The host site (Pampa La Bola, Atacama Astronomical Park) was announced on 12 August 2024.
intervals.quote: Today, July 1st 2019, 39 research institutions from nine countries signed the agreement for the creation of a new international R&D collaboration for a future wide field-of-view gamma ray observatory in the southern hemisphere.

quantity.display: hundreds of GeV to the PeV scale
quantity.note: Stated as "100s of GeV up to the PeV scale"; no numeric bounds are given on the page. The minimum of 100 GeV is the lower end of "100s of GeV" and the maximum of 1,000,000 GeV is 1 PeV; both are order-of-magnitude readings, not figures the page prints.
quantity.quote: Covering an energy range from 100s of GeV up to the PeV scale.

name: SWGO
notes: Status is proposed as of 2026-10-26: the August 2024 site announcement expected "official efforts at the chosen site towards the construction of the SWGO detectors ... as early as 2026" and gamma-ray observations "before the end of the decade", both plans; no source consulted reports that construction has started.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

SWGO is complementary to the southern CTAO array (the SWGO page: "neighbours with the southern array of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory"); no lineage row is written because the sources describe synergy, not succession.

physics_goals.quote: Access to the Galactic Centre and complementary with the major facility CTA-South are key motivations for such a gamma-ray observatory in the south.
physics_goals.value: Map large-scale gamma-ray emission and give full-sky access to transient and variable multi-wavelength and multi-messenger phenomena from the southern hemisphere, including the Galactic Centre; study cosmic rays including anisotropy.

summary.plain: A planned array of water tanks on a high plateau in Chile that would watch most of the southern sky for the most energetic gamma rays, day and night. The site is chosen, but the array is not yet built.
summary.technical: Proposed ground-level-particle gamma-ray observatory for the southern hemisphere: a water-Cherenkov array at 4770 m in the Atacama Astronomical Park, Chile, with a high fill-factor core and a sparse outer array, covering hundreds of GeV to the PeV scale with close to 100% duty cycle and a field of view of order a steradian. Collaboration formed July 2019; site selected August 2024.

unique_capabilities.quote: SWGO is an international effort to construct the first wide-field instrument in the south with deep sensitivity from 100s of GeV into the PeV domain.
unique_capabilities.value: A wide-field, near-100% duty-cycle gamma-ray observatory based on ground-level particle detection, intended to be the first of its kind with access to the southern sky.
